VibePascal -- notes for CONSUMERS of the Linux compiler
Written cy1115 (2026-09-11).  Mirrored into no tarball on purpose, so it can be
corrected without contradicting bytes that are already published.

================================================================
DO NOT INVOKE THE COMPILER FROM ITS OWN SOURCE DIRECTORY
================================================================

Run the Linux compiler from a directory that contains NO .pas files.

    good:  $VP_DIR/bin/ppcx64          <- what the dist tarballs give you
    bad:   $VP_DIR/compiler/ppcx64     <- the build output, sitting in its own source tree

FPC appends the running binary's own directory to the unit search path, after
everything the caller passed.  That is documented, long-standing, correct
behaviour and it is the right thing for a compiler building its own RTL -- there
is no compiler bug here and nothing about it is going to change.

The consequence is entirely about WHERE THE BINARY LIVES.  `make -C compiler`
writes ppcx64 into compiler/, which also holds 207 .pas files.  So anyone who
invokes $VP_DIR/compiler/ppcx64 by that path silently gets 207 of the
compiler's own units prepended to their search path.  They never asked for
them, and nothing in the output says they are there.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY COSTS
----------------------
Measured against a Lazarus tree: 3 of our 207 unit names collide with its 4017
-- `compiler`, `macho`, `tokens`.  That is a small surface, and one of them
fires.  Lazarus has components/fpdebug/macho.pas (2101 lines); we have
compiler/macho.pas (2106 lines).  LazDebuggerFp gets fpdebug's OUTPUT directory
on its unit path but not fpdebug's SOURCE directory, so while that package
compiles, the only macho.pas FPC can see is OURS.  It recompiles unit `macho`
into LazDebuggerFp's output directory with a different CRC (62128 B vs
62168 B), which invalidates fpimgreadermachofile.ppu, and the IDE build dies:

    Fatal: (10022) Can't find unit FpImgReaderMachoFile used by FpImgReaderMacho

The failure names a LAZARUS unit and reads like a Lazarus problem from end to
end.  It cost LazarusDeveloper three cycles and a completely unbuildable
x86_64-linux/gtk2 IDE before a -vut trace showed the real line:

    Searching file .../vibepascal/compiler/macho.pas... found

Same binary, copied into an empty directory, everything else identical: rc=0.
If you are chasing a "can't find unit" whose named unit plainly exists in your
own tree, run with -vut and grep the trace for vibepascal/compiler.

WHAT WE SHIP, AND WHAT YOU HAVE TO DO
-------------------------------------
THE PUBLISHED TARBALLS WERE NEVER AFFECTED.  Every Linux dist tarball
(linux64, aarch64-linux, arm-linux, and the two -cross ones) has shipped
bin/ppc* with ZERO .pas members since v54, exactly like the win64 tarball.
Unpack one and use $VP_DIR/bin/<name> and this cannot reach you.

The exposure is the GIT CHECKOUT used as $VP_DIR, where the binary is a build
product living next to its own sources and where bin/ does not exist at all.
For that case, run:

    dist/linux-bin-layout.sh            # populate <tree>/bin from <tree>/compiler
    dist/linux-bin-layout.sh --check    # verify only; touches nothing

It copies the consumer-facing compilers (ppcx64, ppcross386, ppcrossa64,
ppcrossarm, and the ppcrossaarch64 alias) into <tree>/bin, then PROVES the
property by compiling a trivial program through the installed binary and
asserting the compiler source directory is absent from its unit path -- with
the negative control run first, so a pass cannot be vacuous.
Exit 0 = clean, 1 = the tree is bad, 2 = the check itself could not run.

TWO THINGS THAT LOOK LIKE SHORTCUTS AND ARE NOT
-----------------------------------------------
A SYMLINK DOES NOT WORK.  FPC resolves the executable to its target before
computing exepath, so bin/ppcx64 -> ../compiler/ppcx64 prints
"Using unit path: .../vibepascal/compiler/" and reproduces the hazard in full.
Measured: 20 hits via the symlink, identical to running the original; 0 via a
real copy.  A hard link fails the other way -- a rebuild writes a new inode, so
the link silently stops tracking the compiler you just built.

Which means the copies GO STALE.  bin/ is in .gitignore (upstream FPC's, twice),
so its contents are not committed and cannot be; re-running
linux-bin-layout.sh after a compiler build is part of the deal, and --check
reports a stale copy by md5 rather than letting you ship the wrong compiler.
